title: Simulation of a Run by Total Cost
statement: Let $M$ and $N$ be multi-tape Turing machines, let $e$ map configurations of $M$ to configurations of $N$, let $q$ assign a natural-number cost to each configuration of $M$, and let $X$ and $X'$ be sets of optional states of $M$ and $N$, respectively. Suppose that whenever a configuration $c$ of $M$ has state outside $X$, running $N$ from $e(c)$ for $q(c)$ steps yields $e$ of the one-step successor of $c$ under $M$; configurations with state in $X$ encode to configurations whose state lies in $X'$, and every run of $N$ from $e(c)$ stays outside $X'$ at all times strictly less than $q(c)$ when $c$ has state outside $X$. If a configuration $d$ of $M$ has state outside $X$ at each time $u<t$ in its run, then running $N$ from $e(d)$ for the sum of the costs of the first $t$ configurations in that run yields the encoding of the configuration reached by $M$ after $t$ steps.
